title: intent st attach does not go through the attachment naming gate, so canon can hold a name the address layer refuses
body:
`intent st attach` does not go through the attachment naming gate, so canon can hold an attachment whose name the address layer refuses. Found by cc while building 0461's fix (T4), on 2026-09-19.

**Driven on 3.1.0 (11ce80ad5), in a scratch project:** `intent st attach ST0001 WP/_superseded/01/info.md --from <file>` and `intent st attach ST0001 todo.md --from <file>` both succeed, although `address::parse` refuses both names (`intent:///threads/ST0001/attachments/todo.md` answers as a view). So the thread carries an attachment that no address can reach. What the ingest and the prune then do with such a name has not been driven.

**Where, read from the code at fa4841fd3:**

- `render.rs`'s `st attach` arm builds `Entity::Attachment { thread, path }` directly rather than parsing a spelled address (its comment: "THE ADDRESS IS CONSTRUCTED, NOT SPELLED"), so `parse`'s view check never sees the name.
- The naming gate is `project::attachment_name`, called from `Facade::put` (facade.rs, the attachment arm) and from the ingest's bucket walk (project.rs). The attach path does not reach it.

**Relation to 0461:** 0461's fix (T4) moves `parse`, so a view basename below the thread root is addressable when `classify` calls it an attachment. The thread root stays a view's depth, so a root `todo.md` stays unaddressable, and `st attach` would still write it. 0461's body line "`intent st attach` refuses the name" is false on 3.1.0, and 0461's close note says so.

**Fix direction:** `st attach` runs the same `attachment_name` gate before it writes, and refuses a name the address layer cannot reach, with a remedy naming a legal name. One gate for every door that names an attachment. Then an arm: every door that writes an attachment refuses what `parse` refuses. S.

## Correction (cc, 2026-09-20, driven on the pair at 3a734cde3 with T2 and T4 in it)

**The defect stands, and its evidence narrows to one name.** Re-driven in a scratch project, both halves this time:

- `intent st attach ST0001 todo.md --from <file>` answers `ok: todo.md written to ST0001`, and the spelled door refuses the same name: `intent set intent:///threads/ST0001/attachments/todo.md content --from <file>` answers "`todo.md` is a VIEW, and views have no address". One name, two doors, opposite answers, on one build. That is the defect.
- `intent st attach ST0001 WP/_superseded/01/info.md --from <file>` also succeeds, and `parse` NO LONGER REFUSES IT: through the spelled door it gets past the address layer and fails on the field instead ("`content` ... not a field of this entity"). `view_segment` (address.rs) refuses a view basename below the thread root only when `Project::classify` calls it a generated view, and it does not call this one that. **T4 (0461, landed 80d93de1c) made that name legal**, so attaching it is correct behaviour rather than the fault, and the sentence above claiming `parse` refuses both names is true only of the build it was driven on (3.1.0, 11ce80ad5). It is left standing as the record of that drive rather than rewritten.
- Control, unchanged: `intent st attach ST0001 acceptance.md` is already refused, by `edit_disposition` rather than by the naming gate. So the gap is not that attach admits every view; it is the narrower one that attach's checks and `parse`'s disagree at the THREAD ROOT, for names `classify` does not call generated views.

**What this does to the fix: nothing, and that is the point.** `Facade::put_attachment` (facade.rs) runs `attachment_path_fault`, `edit_disposition`, `classify` and the size cap, and does not run `project::attachment_name`; `Facade::put`, the spelled door, does run it, under a comment saying that sharing the gate is what keeps the two doors accepting the same set. Calling `attachment_name` from `put_attachment` therefore refuses `todo.md` and ACCEPTS `WP/_superseded/01/info.md`, because the gate round-trips the name through `parse` rather than holding a second opinion about it. Both directions are now driven rather than assumed, and the arm asserts both.


CLOSED 2026-09-20, by the landing at e8be15b0f, patch-id e45e2649b8631945b48ce1b83dd0ec18f7769611 read back off the committed tree and identical to the judged bank (refs/bank/cc/0490/patch, blob 1823ac129a52434add1674fa121037aacb7bec7a). Two files, 73 insertions, no deletions: `Facade::put_attachment` calls `project::attachment_name`, placed after `attachment_path_fault` and before the view and canon refusals, which is `Facade::put`'s own precedence; and two arms in `attachment_path_must_name_a_place_in_the_thread.rs`. The coordinator is untouched -- `render.rs` still builds the `Entity` rather than spelling a URL, so the gate lives at the facade where both doors reach it.

**The control, driven to both verdicts:** with the fix reverted and the arms unchanged, `a_root_view_name_is_refused_by_the_gate_the_spelled_door_uses` fails with "this path must be refused: Moved" -- the write had landed and moved the row -- while `a_view_basename_below_the_thread_root_is_still_written` passes. So the refusal arm is load-bearing and the acceptance arm guards against a fix drawn too wide, which is what T4 made necessary. Both arms also assert the two doors agree by calling `attachment_name` directly, so a later drift in either direction reds rather than passing silently.

Suites on the rebase onto b9733bb3d, in a private worktree under an isolated HOME with an in-tree `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`: intentsvcs 297 and 1515 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored; intent-cli 321, 1 and 717 passed, 0 failed. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` clean on both files; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean.

**What is NOT claimed:** the issue's last open question -- what the ingest and the prune do with a badly-named attachment already in canon -- is unchanged by this. The gate stops a new one arriving through `st attach`; a row written before this landing is still there, and `attachment_name` refusing it at ingest is the pre-existing behaviour described in `attachment_naming_gate.rs`, which carries the not-retroactive rule and its reasoning.
